title: Valmiki gets divine guidance to compile the epic
introduction: The scheming of the composition of epic Ramayana is described here. Whole of the epic is rendered in its quintessence, as to how Sage Valmiki scheduled the narration of important milestones of the epic.
closing: इति वाल्मीकिरामायणे आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे तृतीयः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 3rd chapter in Bala Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
श्रुत्वा वस्तु समग्रं तद्धर्मात्मा धर्मसंहितम् |
व्यक्तमन्वेषते भूयो यद् वृत्तं तस्य धीमतः
verses.iast:
śrutvā vastu samagram tat dharma ardha sahitam hitam |
vyak{}tam anveśhate bhūyo yadvṛttam tasya dhīmataḥ
verses.translation: On hearing the essence of Ramayana from Sage Narada, which is abound with probity and prosperity, and a propitious one too, that virtue-souled Valmiki started searching for further known details in the legend of that dexterous Rama.

glosses.meaning: essence of the epic, in its entirety
that which is known [in detail,] further, searched for.

verses.devanagari:
उपस्पृश्योदकं सम्यक् मुनिः स्थित्वा कृताञ्जलिः |
प्राचीनाग्रेषु दर्भेषु धर्मेणान्वेषते गतिम्
verses.iast:
upaspṛsya udakam saṃyak muniḥ sthitvā kṛtāñjaliḥ |
prācīna agreśhu darbheśhu dharmeṇa anveśhate gatim
verses.translation: Valmiki sitting on a sacred grass mat, whose apices are towards east, touched waters, and made his palms adjoined in reverence, and then by his yogic insight started to search comprehensively, for the narrative course of Ramayana.
notes: Comment: Touching/sipping waters ācamana, pariṣecana , before undertaking any auspicious work, including daily meal, is customary, because water cleanses the internal system, both mind and body.

verses.devanagari:
रामलक्ष्मणसीताभी राज्ञा दशरथेन च |
सभार्येण सराष्ट्रेण यत्प्राप्तं तत्र तत्त्वतः
हसितं भाषितं चैव गतिर्या यच्च चेष्टितम् |
तत्सर्वं धर्मवीर्येण यथावत्सम्प्रपश्यति
verses.iast:
rāma lakśmaṇa sītābhiḥ rājñā daśarathena ca |
sa bhāryeṇa sa rāśhṭreṇa yat prāptam tatra tattvataḥ
hasitam bhāśhitam ca eva gatiryāyat ca ceśhṭitam |
tat sarvam dharma vīryeṇa yathāvat samprapaśyati
verses.translation: Of Rama, Lakshmana and Seetha, also of King Dasharatha and his wives, and what bechanced on Rama when he was in kingdom Ayodhya; Valmiki veritably discerned all that. Their smiles, their conversations, their deeds and the succession of events as well, all of them the sage saw wholly and clearly by the yogic power conferred by Brahma...] [1-3-3-4]

glosses.meaning: along with, wife - Rama along with his wife
along with, kingdom - when Rama was in State
their smiles, their conversations, also, thus
by the power of his ascesis, or by the power given by Brahma

verses.devanagari:
स्त्रीतृतीयेन च तथा यत्प्राप्तं चरता वने |
सत्यसंधेन रामेण तत्सर्वं चान्ववेक्षितम्
verses.iast:
strī tṛtīyena ca tathā yat prāptam caratā vane |
satyasandhena rāmeṇa tatsarvam ca anvavekśata
verses.translation: Then, that which bechanced on truth-abiding Rama, while he is trekking in forests, with a lady being the third partner, where Lakshmana is the lone male aide, Valmiki visualized all that.

glosses.meaning: lady, as third [partner in forests,] also

verses.devanagari:
ततः पश्यति धर्मात्मा तत्सर्वं योगमास्थितः |
पुरा यत्तत्र निर्वृत्तं पाणावामलकं यथा
verses.iast:
tataḥ paśyati dharmātmā tat sarvam yogamāsthitaḥ |
purā yat tatra ni.rvṛttam pāṇāva āmalakam yathā
verses.translation: Then that virtue-souled sage saw what all that has happened earlier, by his yogic exaltation, as though it is a citric fruit in his own palm.

verses.devanagari:
तत्सर्वं तत्त्वतो दृष्ट्वा धर्मेण स महामतिः |
अभिरामस्य रामस्य चरितं कर्तुमुद्यतः
कामार्थगुणसंयुक्तं धर्मार्थगुणविस्तरम् |
समुद्रमिव रत्नाढ्यं सर्वश्रुतिमनोहरम्
verses.iast:
tat sarvam tāttvato dṛśṭvā dharmeṇa sa mahāmatiḥ
abhirāmasya rāmasya tat sarvam kartum udyataḥ
kāmārtha guṇa saṃyuk{}tam dharmārtha guṇa vistaram |
samudram iva ratnāḍhyam sarva śruti manoharam
verses.translation: Discerning all of Ramayana in its actuality by his yogic prowess that highly intellectual Valmiki pioneered to author all of the legend of Rama, for Rama is a delighter of all in all worlds, and whose legend is abounding with the real functional qualities of earthly pleasures and prosperities, and which clearly elaborates the meaning of probity and its operative qualities, and thus this legend is like an ocean replete with such gems called thoughts, and an ear-pleasing legend, as well.
notes: Comment: The pleasures and gains of the humans are puruṣārtha -s, in its axiological meaning. Hindus have four such puruṣārtha -s [namely human values,] dharma probity artha prosperity, kāma pleasures, and finally mokśa , blessedness. Of these four only the first three, dharma, artha, kāma are usually referred, and they are called tri-varga . The final one mokśa is not often quoted. Dhrama is the driving force. codanā lakśaṇārtho dharmaḥ - Jaimini. Hence dharma is the prescribed conduct, either by scriptures or by the society, and it does not entail any merit or demerit, but just an obligatory conduct or duty or, say 'categorical imperative' of Kant. And the other two, artha, kāma , are the means of dharma, and all leading to moksha. These two great epics Ramayana and Mahabharata are structured on these puruṣārtha -s alone. Thus though Ramayana is abounding with the accounts of richness and glory of all kinds of wealth, which is secondary to human values, its main import is the virtuosity of human living. The ocean, though abounding with other less valuable items like conch shells, mother-of-pearl shells etc., its gems beneath all these peripherals are of high value. Thus this is an ear pleasing by its musical melody and heart pleasing by its meaningful wording. Further, it is pleasant for its import is in accordance with all the scriptures.

glosses.meaning: pleasures, prosperities, their qualities, abounding with
probity [alone,] its meaning, [and its] qualities, elaborately
for all, listenable, delightfully [or by all Veda-s acceptable, or in any kind of listening, a pleasing one
one who delights all, of such a Rama

verses.devanagari:
स यथा कथितं पुर्वं नारदेन महात्मना |
रघुवंशस्य चरितं चकार भगवान्मुनिः
verses.iast:
sa yathā kathitam pūrvam nāradena mahātmanā |
raghu vaṃśasya caritam cakāra bhagavān muniḥ
verses.translation: That godly saint Valmiki composed the legend of Rama, the legatee of Raghu, exactly as the divine-soul Narada narrated it earlier.

glosses.meaning: one who is born in Raghu's lineage - of Rama

verses.devanagari:
जन्म रामस्य सुमहद् वीर्यं सर्वानुकूलताम् |
लोकस्य प्रियतां क्षान्तिं सौम्यतां सत्यशीलताम्
verses.iast:
janma rāmasya sumahad vīryam sarvānukūlatām |
lokasya priyatām kśāntim sauṃyatām satya śīlatām
verses.translation: The birth of Rama as an incarnation of Vishnu, his very great valour, his gracefulness to all, his universal cordiality, perseverance, courteousness, and his truthful conduct, Valmiki described them all.

verses.devanagari:
नानाचित्रकथाश्चान्या विश्वामित्रसमागमे |
जानक्याश्च विवाहं च धनुषश्च विभेदनम्
verses.iast:
nānā citra kathāḥ ca anyāḥ viśvāmitra sahāyena |
jānakyāḥ ca vivāham ca dhanuṣaḥ ca vibhedanam
verses.translation: Narrated are very many other amusing stories, Rama's breaking the great bow; his marriage with Janaki after with the help of Sage Vishvamitra...

glosses.meaning: other, very many, amusing, stories, also

verses.devanagari:
रामरामविवादं च गुणान्दाशरथेस्तथा |
तदाभिषेकं रामस्य कैकेय्या दुष्टभावताम्
verses.iast:
rāma rāma vivādam ca guṇān dāśaratheḥ tathā |
tatha'bhiśhekam rāmasya kaikeyyā duśhṭa bhāvatām
verses.translation: Dispute of Rama and Parashurama; the merits of Rama, the son of Dasharatha; and the preparations for anointing of Rama as crown prince; Queen Kaikeyi's vicious intentions...
notes: Comment: Rama is śrī rāma one who delights in śrī , where śrī is Goddess Lakshmi. Where as Parashurama delights in his axe paraśu axe; and Balarama, the brother of Krishna delights in his own bala might.

verses.devanagari:
विघातं चाभिषेकस्य रामस्य च विवासनम् |
राज्ञः शोकविलापं च परलोकस्य चाश्रयम्
verses.iast:
vighātam ca abhiśhekasya rāghavasya vivāsanam |
rājñaḥ śokam vilāpam ca para lokasya ca āśrayam
verses.translation: Disruption in royal unction of Raghava; his exile to forests; King Dasharatha's grief and bewailing, and thus his departing to other worlds...

glosses.meaning: into other, world, also, taking shelter [demise.]

verses.devanagari:
प्रकृतीनां विषादं च प्रकृतीनां विसर्जनम् |
निषादाधिपसंवादं सूतोपावर्तनं तथा
verses.iast:
prakṛtīnām viśhādam ca prakṛtīnām visarjanam |
niśhāda adhipa saṃvādam sūtopāvartanam tathā
verses.translation: The grief of the subjects; Rama leaving them off; his conversing with tribal chief Guha; returning the charioteer Sumantra to kingdom from forests, leaving the trio at the banks of river Ganga... all these elements are well- described.

verses.devanagari:
गङ्गायाश्चापि संतारं भरद्वाजस्य दर्शनम् |
भरद्वाजाभ्यनुज्ञानाच्चित्रकूटस्य दर्शनम्
verses.iast:
gañgāyāḥ ca api santāram bharadvājasya darśanam |
bharadvāja abhyanujñāt citrakūṭasya darśanam
verses.translation: Crossing over River Ganga; looking up Sage Bharadwaja; their look up at Chitrakuta on Sage Bharadwaja's advise...

glosses.meaning: River Ganga, also, even, crossing over

verses.devanagari:
वास्तुकर्म निवेशं च भरतागमनं तथा |
प्रसादनं च रामस्य पितुश्च सलिलक्रियाम्
verses.iast:
vāstu karma niveśam ca bharata agamanam tathā |
prasādanam ca rāmasya pituḥ ca salila kriyām
verses.translation: Construction of a hermitage and dwelling therein; Bharata's arrival at that place for the graciousness of Rama to take back the kingdom; Rama's denial of it; Rama's offering water oblations to his father on hearing the demise of his father...

glosses.meaning: architectural, work [construction of hermitage,] dwelling in

verses.devanagari:
पादुकाग्र्याभिषेकं च नन्द्रिग्रामनिवासनम् |
दण्डकारण्यगमनं विराधस्य वधं तथा
verses.iast:
pādukā agrya abhiśhekam ca nandi grāma nivāsanam |
daṇḍakāraṇya gamanam virādhasya vadham tathā
verses.translation: Enthroning shoe-sandals of Rama by Bharata; Bharata's living in a village Nandigrama; Rama's going to Dandaka forests; killing the demon named Viradha...

glosses.meaning: in Nandigrama, village, living of Bharata

verses.devanagari:
दर्शनं शरभङ्गस्य सुतीक्ष्णेन समागमम् |
अनसूयासमाख्यां च अङ्गरागस्य चार्पणम्
verses.iast:
darśanam śarabhañgasya sutīkśṇena samāgamam |
anasūyā samākhyā ca añgarāgsya ca arpaṇam
verses.translation: Rama's visit to Sage Sarabhanga and Suteekshna; their visiting hermitic lady Anasuuya, and her smooth speaking with Seetha and also her giving a body cream to Seetha...[by applying which cream Seetha will not wither away in the rough weather of woods. These details are incorporated with great care.]

glosses.meaning: Anasuya, the hermitic lady, smooth, speaking, also

verses.devanagari:
दर्शनं चाप्यगस्त्यस्य धनुषो ग्रहणं तथा |
शुर्पणख्याश्च संवादं विरुपकरणं तथा
verses.iast:
darśanam ca api agastyasya dhanuṣo grahaṇam tathā |
śūrpaṇakhāḥ ca saṃvādam virūpakaraṇam tathā
verses.translation: Also even Rama's seeing the Sage Agastya, and likewise taking a great bow from that sage... also the palaver of Surpanakha, the demoness, and defacing her, likewise...

verses.devanagari:
वधं खरत्रिशिरसोरुत्थानं रावणास्य च |
मारीचस्य वधं चैव वैदेह्या हरणं तथा
verses.iast:
vadham kharaḥ triśirasaḥ utthānam rāvaṇasya ca |
mārīcasya vadham ca eva vaidehyā haraṇam tathā
verses.translation: The elimination of demons like Khara, Trishirasa and the upsurge of Ravana thereby, elimination of demon Mareecha, and Ravana's abduction of Vaidehi, likewise...

verses.devanagari:
राघवस्य विलापं च गृध्रराजनिबर्हणम् |
कबन्धदर्शनं चैव पम्पायाश्चापि दर्शनम्
verses.iast:
rāghavasya vilāpam ca gṛdhra rāja nibarhaṇam |
kabandha darśanam ca eva pampāyāḥ ca api darśanam
verses.translation: Raghava's anguish at the loss of Seetha; Ravana's slaying the mighty eagle Jatayu; Rama's seeing Kabandha, and also Lake Pampa...

glosses.meaning: Kabandha, the demon, is seen, also, thus
Pampa, the lake, also, thus, seeing.

verses.devanagari:
शबरीदर्शनं चैव फलमूलाशनं तथा |
प्रलापं चैव पम्पायां हनुमद्दर्शनं तथा
verses.iast:
śabarī darśanam ca eva phala mūla aśanam tathā |
pralāpam ca eva pampāyam hanumad darśanam
verses.translation: Rama's seeing Shabari, a hermetic lady and eating fruits and tubers given by her in utmost adoration; Rama's bemoaning for Seetha; his sighting Hanuma at Lake Pampa...

glosses.meaning: Sabari, the hermitic lady, seeing her, also, thus
at Pampa Lake, Hanuma, sighted at.

verses.devanagari:
ऋष्यमूकस्य गमनं सुग्रीवेण समागमम् |
प्रत्ययोत्पादनं सख्यं वालिसुग्रीवविग्रहम्
verses.iast:
ṛśhyamūkasya gamanam sugrīveṇa samāgamam |
pratyayotpādanam sakhyam vāli sugrīva vigraham
verses.translation: Also going to Mt. Rishyamuka, meeting Sugreeva and generating confidence in Sugreeva, befriending him and the duel of Vali and Sugreeva...

verses.devanagari:
वालिप्रमथनं चैव सुगीवप्रतिपादनम् |
ताराविलापं समयं वर्षरात्रनिवासनम्
verses.iast:
vāli pramathanam ca eva sugīva pratipādanam |
tārā vilāpam samayam varśha rātra nivāsanam
verses.translation: Also thus Vali's elimination and establishing Sugreeva on throne of monkey kingdom, grieving of Tara, the wife of Vali and empress of that kingdom, and as consented Rama's stopover during the days of rain...
notes: Comment: This rātri usually means night. But it includes day also. When saying trirātra, daśa rātra, in conducting rituals it includes daytime also. On the whole it is total rainy season that is admirably narrated in Kishkindha Kanda.

verses.devanagari:
कोपं राघवसिंहस्य बलानामुपसंग्रहम् |
दिशः प्रस्थापनं चैव पृथिव्याश्च निवेदनं
verses.iast:
kopam rāghava siṃhasya balānām upasaṅgraham |
diśaḥ prasthāpanam ca eva pṛthivyāḥ ca nivedanam
verses.translation: The wrath of Raghava, the lion, at the delay caused by Sugreeva, and Sugreeva's foregathering of all troops, and sending them to all quarters, and Sugreeva's description of earth's topography to monkey-troops...

verses.devanagari:
अङ्गुलीयकदानं च ऋक्षस्य बिलदर्शनम् |
प्रायोपवेशनं चापि सम्पातेश्चापि दर्शनम्
verses.iast:
añgulīyaka dānam ca ṛkśsya bila darśanam |
prāyopaveśanam ca api sampāteḥ ca api darśanam
verses.translation: Rama's giving his ring to Hanuma as a token for Seetha's recognition... and the monkeys thus searching see Riskha cave, bear-cave, and their fasting unto death for their quest remained unsuccessful, and their seeing Sampaati, another mighty eagle and the brother of slain Jatayu, who guides the monkeys to the destination where Seetha is held capitive.

glosses.meaning: ring of his finger, giving, also

verses.devanagari:
पर्वतारोहणं चापि सागरस्यापि लङ्घनम् |
समुद्रवचनाच्चैव मैनाकस्य च दर्शनम्
verses.iast:
parvata ārohaṇam ca api sāgarsya api lañghanam |
samudra vacanāt ca eva mainākasya ca darśanam
verses.translation: Hanuma's climbing Mt. Mahendra to leap over the ocean, and on the advice of the Ocean, Mt. Mainaka's coming up from under waters to give rest to Hanuma, and Hanuma's seeing that mountain are depicted.

glosses.meaning: of ocean, also, leaping out of

verses.devanagari:
राक्षसीतर्जनं चैव छायाग्राहस्य दर्शनम् |
सिंहिकायाश्च निधनं लङ्कामलयदर्शनम्
verses.iast:
rākśasī tarjanam ca eva chāyā grāhasya darśanam |
siṃhikāyāḥ ca nidhanam lañkā malaya darśanam
verses.translation: Hanuma's killing the demoness Surasa, and his seeing of Simhika, a rapacious creature of gigantic origin, which captures its prey by the shadow, and Hanuma's killing that Simhika, and his seeing the mountain of Lanka, called Mt. Trikuta, on which the state of Lanka is built, Valmiki described them all.

glosses.meaning: seeing, Simhika, the capturer by shadow, seeing her

verses.devanagari:
रात्रौ लङ्काप्रवेशं च एकस्याथ विचिन्तनम् |
आपानभूमिगमनमवरोधस्य दर्शनम्
verses.iast:
rātrau laṅkā praveśam ca ekasya api vicintanam |
āpāna bhūmi gamanam avarodhasya darśanam
verses.translation: In night Hanuma's entry into Lanka, for being lonely his thinking over the course to search for Seetha, and his going to the liquor consumption place, and also his seeing the palace chambers of Ravana...

glosses.meaning: of secure place, [the palace chambers,] seeing.

verses.devanagari:
दर्शनं रावणस्यापि पुष्पकस्य च दर्शनम् |
अशोकवनिकायानं सीतायाश्चापि दर्शनम्
verses.iast:
darśanam rāvaṇasya api puśhpakasya ca darśanam |
aśoka vanikāyānam sītāyāḥ ca api darśanam
verses.translation: Hanuma's seeing Ravana, and also his seeing Pushpaka, the divine aircraft, and in Ashoka gardens, his seeing Seetha also...

verses.devanagari:
अभिज्ञानप्रदानं च सीतायाश्चापि भाषणम् |
राक्षसीतर्जनं चैव त्रिजटास्वप्नदर्शनम्
verses.iast:
abhijñana pradānam ca sītāyāḥ ca api bhāṣaṇam |
rākśasī tarjanam ca eva trijaṭā svapna darśanam
verses.translation: Presenting his credential, the ring of Rama, to Seetha and his talk with Seeta, and also his witnessing the demonesses scaring Seetha to oblige Ravana, and his witnessing demoness Trijata narrating her bad dream, are all narrated in the epic.]

verses.devanagari:
मणिप्रदानं सीताया वृक्षभङ्गं तथैव च |
राक्षसीविद्रवं चैव किंकराणां निबर्हणम् |
verses.iast:
maṇi pradānam sītāyāḥ vṛkśa bhaṅgam tatha eva ca |
rākśasī vidravam caiva kiṅkarāṇām nibarhaṇam |
verses.translation: Seetha's giving her bejeweled hairslide to be shown to Rama, Hanuma's uprooting of the trees of that beautiful Ashoka gardens, thereby the demonesses fleeing in scare, his killing the guards of that garden...

verses.devanagari:
ग्रहणं वायुसूनोश्च लङ्कादाहाभिगर्जनम् |
प्रतिप्लवनमेवाथ मधूनां हरणं तथा
verses.iast:
grahaṇam vāyu sūnośca laṅkā dāha abhigarjanam |
prati plavanam eva atha madhūnām haraṇam tathā
verses.translation: The capture of Hanuma, the son of Air-god, by the magical missile of Indrajit, son of Ravana, and also Hanuma's burning down Lanka, and his blaring at the demons, also his return flight from Lanka... and on his way back Hanuma's seeing a honey garden, and the appropriation of honey...

glosses.meaning: capture of, son of Vayu, Air-god, also
Lanka, burning of, [and his blaring at demons]

verses.devanagari:
राघवाश्वासनं चैव मणिनिर्यातनं तथा |
सङ्गमं च समुद्रेण नलसेतोश्च बन्धनम्
verses.iast:
rāghava āsvāsanam caiva maṇi niryātanam tathā |
saṅgamam ca samudreṇa nala setoḥ ca bandhanam
verses.translation: Hanuma's action in presenting the jewel sent by Seetha solaces Raghava, and thus the meeting of Rama with the Ocean, and Nala's building the bridge on ocean...

verses.devanagari:
प्रतारं च समुद्रस्य रात्रौ लङ्कावरोधनम् |
विभीषणेन संसर्गं वधोपायनिवेदनम्
verses.iast:
pratāram ca samudrasya rātrau laṅkā avarodhanam |
vibhīśhaṇena saṃsargam vadhopāya nivedanam
verses.translation: Crossing over the ocean by the boulder bridge built by Nala, and seizure of Lanka in night, and Vibheeshana, the younger brother of Ravana, whom Ravana banished, comes to meet Rama, and his telling the scheme to kill Ravana to Rama...

glosses.meaning: meeting, with Vibheeshana, killing, scheme, telling.

verses.devanagari:
कुम्भकर्णस्य निधनं मेघनादनिबर्हणम्|
रावणस्य विनाशं च सीतावाप्तिमरेः पुरे
verses.iast:
kumbhakarṇasya nidhanam meghanāda nibarhaṇam |
rāvaṇasya vināśam ca sītāvāptim areḥ pure

glosses.meaning: Seetha, restitution of, in enemy's, city.

verses.devanagari:
वीभीषणाभिषेकं च पुष्पकस्य च दर्शनम् |
अयोध्यायाश्च गमनं भरद्वाजसमागमम्
verses.iast:
vibhīśhaṇa abhiśhekam ca puśhpakasya ca darśanam |
ayodhyāyāḥ ca gamanam bharadvāja samāgamam
verses.translation: Crowning of Vibheeshana as the king of Lanka, after the demise of Ravana, and also Rama's seeing Pushpaka, the divine aircraft, and returning to Ayodhya in that aircraft... and Rama's meeting Sage Bharadvaja on his way back...

verses.devanagari:
प्रेषणं वायुपुत्रस्य भरतेन समागमम् |
रामाभिषेकाभ्युदयं सर्वसैन्यविसर्जनम् |
स्वराष्ट्ररञ्जनं चैव वैदेह्याश्च विसर्जनम्
verses.iast:
preṣaṇam vāyu putrasya bharatena samāgamam |
rāma abhiśheka abhyudayam sarva sainya visarjanam |
sva rāśhṭra rañjanam ca eva vaidehyāḥ ca visarjanam
verses.translation: Sending Hanuma to meet Bharata, for he avowed to self-immolate if Rama were not to come in time; the coronation festival of Rama; disbandment of all military troops of monkeys; Rama's ruling his kingdom to the delight of his subjects, and the desolation of Vaidehi too... are described by Valmiki.

glosses.meaning: own, kingdom, to the delight of State

verses.devanagari:
अनागतं च यत्किञ्चिद्रामास्य वसुधातले |
तच्चकारोत्तरे काव्ये वाल्मीकिर्भगवानृषिः
verses.iast:
anāgatam ca yat kiñcid rāmasya vasudhā tale |
tat cakāra uttare kāvye vālmīkiḥ bhagavān ṛśhiḥ
verses.translation: The godly sage Valmiki composed the futuristic legend of Rama while on the surface of earth, and whatever that is there, that is composed in all its minuteness, in the coming chapters of this epic.
notes: Comment: In this verse, some take the word uttare as Uttara Ramayana, the events occurring after his crowning, Seetha's departure to forest, birth of Lava and Kusha, the sons of Rama and a battle between father and sons etc., are ascribed to Valmiki. But to some commentators, as per the format of this chapter, which surveys what Valmiki has scheduled to write, it is unacceptable since the word uttare occurs for only one occasion, hence cannot mean next canto. Thus, they say, Uttara Ramayana cannot be ascribed to Valmiki. Hence the word uttare here is taken to mean henceforth, hereinafter of the epic.
